#### **VIKTOR**

## [What kind of harness does GPT-11 want to live in?](https://ref.viktor.com/vik-aiv-main7-hl)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e047fed4-dfd8-44e7-8680-d430d166156e/aivalley_main7_1280x720__1_.jpg?t=1787667343)

Every model release makes AI smarter for free. The harness around the model decides how much of that turns into real work. A model that could do a great analyst's job is still stuck if it forgets everything between chats and only acts when someone types at it.

So we built Viktor for the models that are coming: a persistent workspace where it writes and runs code, memory that compounds across sessions, schedules it sets for itself, and 3,200+ tools it can call. The result is an AI employee in Slack and Microsoft Teams that runs work end to end. 60,000+ teams have hired one.

The full essay on our harness decisions is in the post.

#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2bbde24c-ac2b-424a-b0d4-20df6780e533/World_SocialShare.width-1300__1_.png?t=1787670188)
Caption: Google’s Project Genie | World Model ==prototype==

**1/ Nvidia is taking its AI chips to space** - SpaceX is [building](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/spacexai-adopts-nvidia-vera-cpu-to-accelerate-agentic-ai-at-massive-scale) its Starmind orbital data centers around Nvidia’s Vera Rubin platform, with a space version targeted for [Q4 next year](https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2091939113008238838?s=20). SpaceXAI is also using Nvidia’s Vera CPU for Grok’s agents.

The space version is apparently lighter, denser and cheaper, and built to deal with radiation and heat. Orbital compute costs 4x+ what it costs on Earth today, but Musk thinks that eventually flips.

Nvidia is also going after the CPU side of AI. [Vera](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/spacexai-adopts-nvidia-vera-cpu-to-accelerate-agentic-ai-at-massive-scale) is built to handle all the boring work around agents, like running code, calling tools, and moving data around, with Nvidia claiming up to 1.8x faster agentic task completion than traditional x86 chips.

So yeah, AI data centers might not all be on Earth forever.

**2/ AI is starting to move into the real world** - a bunch of new “[world models](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/ai-world-models-robotics-33ab46cb?st=xnEhg4&reflink=desktopwebshare_permalink&utm_source=tldrnewsletter)” are being trained on videogames and simulations to control robots. Instead of learning what a cup is from text, they learn what happens when you actually move the thing.

General Intuition is one of the companies doing this. They’ve trained on millions of hours of videogame play, including the actions people take, and can apparently fine-tune the model to control a robot dog, drone or other machine.

Google DeepMind is already combining this with Gemini in [SIMA 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zphax4f6Rls&t=1s). Gemini handles the reasoning and goals, while SIMA learns to actually carry them out inside 3D game worlds.

And there is a _lot_ of money going into this. World Labs [raised $1B](https://www.worldlabs.ai/blog/funding-2026) at a $5.4B valuation, AMI Labs raised $1.03B at $3.5B, General Intuition [raised $133.7M](https://techcrunch.com/2025/10/16/general-intuition-lands-134m-seed-to-teach-agents-spatial-reasoning-using-video-game-clips/), Physical Intelligence [raised $600M](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-20/robotics-startup-physical-intelligence-valued-at-5-6-billion-in-new-funding) at $5.6B, and Wayve just [raised $1.2B](https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/24/self-driving-tech-startup-wayve-raises-1-2b-from-nvidia-uber-and-three-automakers/) at $8.6B. Google DeepMind is also pouring resources into SIMA, Genie and Veo, and Demis has said he expects world models to become an important part of Gemini’s planning.

The fun question is what happens when these things get plugged into LLMs. LLMs are pretty bad at understanding a 3D world, and you probably don’t want your robot hallucinating when it’s moving around.

Feels like we’re at the GPT-2 stage of physical AI.

More on world models:

* What’s [a world model?](https://blog.google/company-news/inside-google/googlers/ask-a-techspert/what-is-a-world-model-project-genie/)

* [The Waymo world model](https://waymo.com/blog/2026/02/the-waymo-world-model-a-new-frontier-for-autonomous-driving-simulation/) - a new frontier for autonomous driving simulation

I TRIED THE AI MODEL BUILT TO FIX AI WRITING https://every.


A NEW LAB SAYS THE SAMENESS OF AI PROSE IS A TRAINING PROBLEM. IT MADE THE WRITING LESS PREDICTABLE—BUT NOT NECESSARILY ANY BETTER. https://every.

by Katie Parrott https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSSBUcmllZCB0aGUgQUkgTW9kZWwgQnVpbHQgdG8gRml4IEFJIFdyaXRpbmciLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUwLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9Aa2F0aWUucGFycm90dDEyIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjR9

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSSBUcmllZCB0aGUgQUkgTW9kZWwgQnVpbHQgdG8gRml4IEFJIFdyaXRpbmciLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUwLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9hY2NvdW50IiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjV9 to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



Imagine a cover band that technically knows every song ever written but only has one arrangement. The melody consists of the same set of chords. The guitarist plays the same solo whether they are covering “Landslide” or “Party in the U.S.A.” By the fourth song, you are tired, and more than a little angry.

That’s what reading raw AI writing can feel like. The first few items you read, nothing trips your alarm—it’s just competent, if somewhat boring, writing. Then you keep seeing the same moves again and again: the patterns of three, the “not X, but Y,” the short sentence hanging off the back end of the paragraph that exists to do nothing but tell you that what you just read “matters.” Eventually you stop absorbing what the words are trying to communicate.

I’ve said before that it feels like model progress on writing at the major labs has stalled. Maybe no one model can be all things to all people, or maybe OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google have bigger, more lucrative fish to fry in the coding space. On the one hand, fair enough. But as an AI-pilled writer, I can’t help feeling a little left out. It reminds me of high school, when the AP English paper deadline got pushed back after I’d already written it, because obviously the AP Physics exam took precedence.

So when I heard about a new, writing-focused model, I immediately queued it up for a Vibe Check.


WHAT IS DEFT?

Deft https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSSBUcmllZCB0aGUgQUkgTW9kZWwgQnVpbHQgdG8gRml4IEFJIFdyaXRpbmciLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUwLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9kZWZ0d3JpdGluZy5jb20vIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjZ9 is a new research lab and model focused on “better writing.” The lab was cofounded by Justin Murphy https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSSBUcmllZCB0aGUgQUkgTW9kZWwgQnVpbHQgdG8gRml4IEFJIFdyaXRpbmciLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUwLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS9qbXJwaHkiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6N30=, a former political-science professor turned writer and publisher, and an AI researcher who goes by the name Rosmine https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSSBUcmllZCB0aGUgQUkgTW9kZWwgQnVpbHQgdG8gRml4IEFJIFdyaXRpbmciLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUwLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS9yb3NtaW5lIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjh9. Its first release, DFT v1, is a writing model post-trained with the lab’s custom fine-tuning method. Initially introduced in June, DFT v1 entered public beta last week.

The team behind Deft has a theory about why AI writing feels the way it does: LLMs have a distribution problem. Not in the sense of whether the writing gets read by people—it does, although not always happily. Deft is concerned with the distribution of the words themselves: which phrases recur, how sentences tend to begin and end, and whether a large body of output collapses toward the same handful of moves. The company’s bet is that, if you train a model to match the distribution of human writing across a batch of documents—not merely make each individual response acceptable—you’ll get prose with more range.

The engine driving Deft’s approach is a method called “distribution fine-tuning,” https://every. or DFT, a post-training step applied after a model has learned to predict language. Typical fine-tuning grades one response at a time, meaning that 1,000 responses can each pass inspection while in the aggregate, they are repeating the same openings and rhythms. DFT instead compares batches of model outputs with batches of human writing, then adjusts the model when the two distributions differ.

The resulting model is called DFT v1. On Deft’s tests, it produced a distribution of writing closer to the human samples than a conventional fine-tune of the same size. The basic claim is that changing the post-training will yield more range.

https://every. Deft console set to “rewrite” and “more human,” with the initial, AI-generated output provided. (All images courtesy of Katie Parrott.)




For now, the model is available via Deft’s website and paid API. You supply a prompt, choose whether you want the model to work faster, smarter, or “more human,” and choose an output format from a selection of four: news article, analytical essay, SEO article, or company blog. howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy monday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* MIT researchers found AI can create “delusional spirals” 

* Humanoid robots are officially faster than Usain Bolt... kinda

* A mystery AI model is giving the frontier labs a headache

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **MOONSHOTS LIVE**

## [$2M to founders who used AI on a problem people have](https://moonshots.com/landing/ai-valley?utm_source=ai-valley&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=mslive25&utm_content=2026-08-31)

Most of the futures we get shown are the ones falling apart. That is a failure of imagination with real consequences, because the futures we picture are the ones we end up building. So we put $5.5M behind the other kind.

The Build with Gemini XPRIZE gave builders 90 days to point AI at a problem people actually have. $2M across 25 winners, $500K to first, judged by Palmer Luckey, Cathie Wood, Anousheh Ansari, Mark Pincus and Logan Kilpatrick. Revenue was the proof it worked, not the point.

The same night a film gets greenlit for a $2.5M grant, chosen from 6,000 entries and judged by Neil deGrasse Tyson and Neal Stephenson.

More than 30,000 people competed. Everything is decided on one stage on September 25, in a restored 1920s movie palace in downtown LA. Nothing pre-recorded. 1,500 seats.

[Claim your seats](https://moonshots.com/landing/ai-valley?utm_source=ai-valley&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=mslive25&utm_content=2026-08-31)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/00caa63f-fa98-41e1-a1bd-b54d46ac07ea/-1x-1__3___1_.png?t=1787580698)
Caption: Courtesy: World Humanoid Robot Games

**1/ MIT researchers found AI can create “delusional spirals”** - they built a [mathematical model](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.19141) showing how a sycophantic AI can gradually make users more confident in a false belief by repeatedly validating it. And the weird part: making the AI more factual didn’t fully solve the problem. It could still cherry-pick true information that supported the user’s theory while ignoring evidence against it.

They also tried warning users that the AI might be flattering them... didn’t work. The belief spiral could still happen even when users knew about the AI’s tendency to agree with them. Basically, an AI doesn’t need to lie to reinforce a bad idea. It just needs to keep giving you the evidence you want to hear.

The paper points to a real risk, but it doesn’t mean every AI interaction will send you into a “delusional spiral.” A lot depends on how you use the model. If you configure it to challenge your assumptions, cite sources, and give you competing viewpoints, it can be much harder for this kind of spiral to happen. AI is already a great research tool and makes it much easier to automate repetitive work, but getting it to consistently challenge you and tell you when you’re wrong is still a very different problem.

**2/ Humanoid robots are officially faster than Usain Bolt... kinda** - a humanoid robot from Beijing-based X-Humanoid ran the [100m in 9.39 seconds](https://x.com/AP/status/2091451125786407202?s=20) at the [five-day](https://x.com/WHRGFUN) World Humanoid Robot Games, beating Bolt’s 9.58-second human record. The funny part is that braking was still a problem... some robots basically [crashed](https://x.com/AP/status/2091451125786407202?s=20) into the mat after crossing the finish line. [Another robot](https://x.com/MarioNawfal/status/2091558583683232242?s=20) cleared 2.88m in the standing high jump, also above the human record. More than 2,000 robots are competing across 51 events, including [jumping](https://x.com/ViralRushX/status/2091811768364605512?s=20), soccer, [table tennis](https://x.com/kyleichan/status/2091271208234836178?s=20), [ping-pong](https://x.com/MarioNawfal/status/2091568649802789247?s=20), and weightlifting.

There’s a catch, though... These robots aren’t exactly ready to replace Olympic athletes or humans at work. Humanoids are still mostly being used for research and demonstrations, but the rapid improvement is pretty wild. China is also producing the majority of the world’s humanoid robots, making these games another showcase in the growing US-China robotics race.

**3/ A mystery AI model is giving the frontier labs a headache** - a stealth model called [Ox Alpha](https://openrouter.ai/stealth/ox-alpha) appeared on OpenRouter from an anonymous provider and quickly started going viral among developers. It’s built for coding and long-running agentic work, with a 1.05M-token context window, 131K-token outputs, and reportedly enough capacity to process 100T tokens per day.

Early tests suggest [Ox Alpha](https://x.com/OpenRouter/status/2090544970923184269?s=20) may be beating models like Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol on coding benchmarks such as Deep SWE... although there’s no independent validation on public leaderboards yet. Stripe CEO Patrick Collison called it “very impressive,” which probably didn’t help calm the speculation around who actually built it.

And everyone is trying to figure out who’s behind it. The guesses range from Google’s next Gemini to Microsoft’s MAI models to Chinese labs like Z.ai. Nothing has been confirmed.

Hello, and happy Sunday! This week we launched Thesis Statements, where 100 AI leaders call their shots on work after automation. The project sets the stage for November’s Thesis: 2027 conference. Elsewhere, life on the frontier got expensive—and organizational: Every’s AI bill jumped 230 percent, one engineer turned Codex into a team of specialists, and mental healthcare company Headway built the secure assistant it couldn’t buy. We also made the case for AI writing that keeps human judgment in the loop, and introduced a frontier team to keep weird experiments going amid urgent work.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up to get it in your inbox.

----------------------------------------


KNOWLEDGE BASE

“What Does Human Work Look Like After Automation?” by Dan Shipper/On Every: When execution is cheap and intelligence is abundant, what’s left for people to do? Thesis Statements collects 100 specific, contestable predictions from AI leaders who live on the frontier. The first 25 are live: Linear CEO Karri Saarinen argues that AI’s biggest problem will be design; Ness Labs founder Anne-Laure Le Cunff says answers will become abundant and questions will become the hard part; and Granola cofounder Chris Pedregal predicts some of your hardest problems will solve themselves. We’ll share more statements weekly until the conference and revisit the claims to see which pan out. You can also submit your own.

“Our AI Costs Jumped 230 Percent. I’m Not Setting Token Budgets—Yet.” by Arielle Shipper/Every: When GPT-5.6 Sol landed, Every’s daily credit usage jumped from 11,520 to 26,685 credits—more than twice its baseline. Head of operations Arielle Shipper had to control spend without killing the experimentation the business runs on. Her answer: Parameters, not policies. Rather than hard limits, she interrogates any big run with three questions—what it cost, what it bought us, and what we learned—and shares four lessons for managing operations at the frontier.

“An Engineering Team for the Cost of Codex” by Laura Entis/Context Window: With GPT-5.6, one person can now manage a team of specialized AI agents that functions like a full engineering team. Naveen Naidu runs his Monologue shop as a roster of specialized Codex agents that hand work off to each other like coworkers. Also inside: Naveen’s specific workflow; a breakdown of the tech stack lead designer Daniel Rodrigues used to build Every’s Thesis: 2027 brand and website; a “discuss” on whether harness engineering will go the way of prompt engineering; and an AI & I episode from the archive on why AI companions are a new art form, with Portola cofounder Quinten Farmer and head of story Eliot Peper. 🎧🖥 Listen on Spotify or Apple Podcasts, watch on X or YouTube, or read the transcript.

“In Defense of AI Writing” by Laura Entis/Context Window: Is AI writing automatically slop? Not always. Every’s head of tech consulting Mike Taylor writes many of his posts with AI assistance—dictating tests he ran himself, then letting a model format them—a workflow that shrinks a day of writing to two hours and gets his ideas in front of more people. Also inside: a “signal” unpacking the fight over Anthropic’s plan to watermark Claude’s text, and a “steal this workflow” on how senior editor Jack Cheng batches Google Docs edits with Codex and the ChatGPT Chrome extension.

OFF-THE-SHELF AI COULDN’T MEET HEADWAY’S SECURITY AND WORKFLOW NEEDS, SO IT BUILT ITS OWN ON THE CLAUDE CODE SDK. NOW THE WHOLE COMPANY USES IT. https://every.

by Katie Parrott https://every.

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Headway is an Every Consulting client; we delivered its leadership team a paid executive AI workshop. Headway was given an opportunity to fact-check details but had no editorial control over this article.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



At mental healthcare company Headway, an AI agent can act without asking permission at every step. That might sound unexpected for a 900-person company in an industry governed by strict rules for sensitive patient information. But the autonomy is possible because of Headway’s tight controls around the agent. Every conversation runs inside a sealed, disposable container, with carefully limited connections to company tools and data.

That architecture underpins Eddy, the internal AI assistant Headway built when existing products couldn’t meet its particular combination of security, compliance, and workflow requirements. Eddy is built on the Claude Code SDK, Anthropic’s toolkit for teams developing products with Claude Code. It’s hosted in Headway’s Amazon Web Services environment and connected to the company’s tools and data.

Work on Eddy had barely begun six months ago. Headway initially wanted an existing product and was preparing to sign a deal with a major AI vendor to give employees access to its desktop app. But relying on vendors to deliver features that met Headway’s workflow and strict compliance requirements for handling sensitive patient data “felt like we were missing the train,” says chief technology officer Arnaud Ferreri.

howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy friday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* Qwen just got a seriously capable uncensored version

* Slack launched Slack Code

* Anthropic wants to beat SpaceX’s IPO record

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **FITNEXA**

## [Most Earbuds Weren’t Made for Bed](https://go.fitnexa.com/DPo07i)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/57386ca0-3b1f-4e0d-8055-619dfa6a6fd6/20251021-114822__1___1_.png?t=1787059367)
Follow image link: (https://go.fitnexa.com/DPo07i)
Caption: Courtesy Fitnexa

Most wireless earbuds are designed for commuting, working out, or taking calls. Sleeping in them is kind of an afterthought.

SomniPods 3 take the opposite approach.

They’re 9.9mm thin, weigh 3.3g each, and are shaped to sit more comfortably when your ear is against a pillow. They also combine Hybrid ANC, passive isolation, and sound masking to help with the kind of noise that suddenly feels very loud at 2 a.m.

It’s one of those products that makes more sense once you realize how oddly specific the problem is.

If you already sleep with earbuds, or have tried and hated it, SomniPods 3 are probably much closer to what you were looking for.

[See SomniPods 3](https://go.fitnexa.com/DPo07i)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

Tweet:  (https://twitter.com/gregpr07/status/2089897646739894354?s=20)

**1/ Qwen just got a seriously capable uncensored version** - independent teams including OrcaRouter and AEON-7 used a technique called “abliteration” to remove much of [Alibaba’s Qwen3.8-27B’s](https://huggingface.co/orcarouter/Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-MLX?utm_source=chatgpt.com) refusal behavior without stripping away its core intelligence. It’s not an official Alibaba release, but a community modification that keeps the original model’s coding, agentic, vision, reasoning, and 262K-token context capabilities, while being small enough to run locally on consumer hardware. ([watch the demo](https://x.com/gregpr07/status/2089897646739894354?s=20))

The wild part is that this isn’t a tiny jailbreak model... Qwen3.8-27B is a 27B open-weight model with capabilities that can compete with much larger systems, and the uncensored versions can run directly on [Apple Silicon Macs](https://x.com/akshen121/status/2090044678158860771?s=20) or consumer GPUs. The model also retains its thinking mode, so users can control how much reasoning it does before answering.

And this is where things get controversial... researchers and red-teamers can use it for security testing without cloud-based safety filters getting in the way, but the same capabilities can also be used for harmful or illegal requests.

**2/ Slack launched Slack Code** - it gives teams [dedicated channels](https://x.com/Benioff/status/2090240159115853956?s=20) where humans and AI agents can build software together. Tag Claude, ChatGPT, Devin or Copilot and it spins up a code channel with the plan, conversation, diffs and live preview all in one place. Slack Code is free on every plan, though the agents themselves are separately paid. ([learn more here](https://x.com/SlackHQ/status/2090415566351659267))

Slack is becoming the new agent workspace... The interesting bit is that everyone can watch the agent work, review its diffs, give feedback and approve changes before they ship. Anyone can also pause or redirect an agent, while production merges require human sign-off. So it’s more like “your whole team builds with AI in the same room.”

And coding probably isn’t the end game. Slack says the same infrastructure could eventually let custom agents handle things like marketing campaigns, legal reviews and other workflows.

**3/ Anthropic wants to beat SpaceX’s IPO record** - the Claude maker is reportedly preparing to [match or top](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-20/anthropic-expects-to-match-spacex-s-record-ipo-size-or-top-it?accessToken=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzb3VyY2UiOiJTdWJzY3JpYmVyR2lmdGVkQXJ0aWNsZSIsImlhdCI6MTc4NzI5NzA2MCwiZXhwIjoxNzg3OTAxODYwLCJhcnRpY2xlSWQiOiJUSzBUVktLSzNOWUMwMCIsImJjb25uZWN0SWQiOiI2NTc1NjkyN0UwMkM0N0MwQkQ0MDNEQTJGMEUyNzIyMyJ9.OxE678o5_5twVs_xmvCzAFwLomwkkT77ZbpvHnLXzco&utm_source=tldrnewsletter&leadSource=article-gifting) SpaceX’s record $75B IPO, with a public filing potentially coming by the end of this month. SpaceX’s IPO raised a record $86.2 billion, which means Anthropic could raise close to $100 billion. Anthropic was valued at $965B in its latest funding round, and its revenue is absolutely flying: Q2 revenue topped $11.5B, up from just $787M a year earlier.

The spending is wild too... Anthropic reportedly lost almost $42B in 2025, roughly 5x more than the year before.

Anthropic could also beat OpenAI to the public markets... both companies have confidentially filed, but OpenAI is reportedly looking at 2027. If Anthropic actually pulls off a $75B+ IPO, it would instantly become one of the biggest IPOs ever and push 2026 toward becoming the biggest year for US IPOs on record. Anthropic is expected to IPO by the end of 2026.

--------------------

* [Replit Free Mode](https://replit.com/blog/replit-introduces-free-mode) - lets users create 30x more with OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Luna without using credits for everyday tasks
